programme: RFXANK anchors the RFX5–RFXANK–RFXAP/CIITA enhanceosome that drives constitutive and IFN-γ-inducible MHC class II expression (its target list is almost entirely HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO plus CIITA and IFNG itself); MSC represses a cluster of T-cell effector/Treg genes (FOXP3, CTLA4, IL2RA, IL10, IFNG) that determines how the antigen-presenting signal is read out; IRX2's two targets, CXCL10 and CCL5, are the IFN-inducible chemokines that recruit the CXCR3+/CCR5+ lymphocytes able to respond to MHC-II presentation. Together: antigen presentation, T-cell/Treg tone, and lymphocyte trafficking.
role_in_a: In blood, this axis sets how strongly circulating antigen-presenting cells display MHC-II and how the Treg/effector balance and CXCL10/CCL5-driven lymphocyte trafficking are tuned — the kind of systemic immune-regulatory tone that has been proposed (not settled) as part of fibromyalgia's low-grade immune/neuroinflammatory component.
role_in_b: In lower-grade glioma, MHC-II expression on tumor and tumor-associated myeloid cells, Treg/effector gene balance, and CXCL10/CCL5-mediated lymphocyte recruitment are the levers that shape the tumor immune microenvironment — LGG, especially IDH-mutant tumors, is repeatedly described as relatively 'immune-cold', a state this same circuit would produce if suppressed.
shared_axis: If this circuit runs low in both tissues, the two diseases would independently show reduced antigen presentation and lymphocyte recruitment — systemically in blood for fibromyalgia, locally in the tumor bed for glioma — without needing any direct biological link between the two diseases; the shared axis is a shared regulatory logic (MHC-II/Treg/chemokine tone), not a shared pathology.
reasoning: RFXANK's target set is close to a textbook signature of the RFX–CIITA MHC-II enhanceosome, so the module itself is real and nameable; MSC's targets are a recognizable Treg/effector gene set, giving the module a second, less certain leg. But nothing retrieved places this circuit in fibromyalgia or in LGG specifically — Open Targets shows no association for any of the three factors in either disease, and the only papers retrieved for the wider factor list are either off-topic (colorectal cancer for TCF12, an inconclusive glioblastoma mention for HEY1 — neither of which is a carrying factor here) or keyword collisions (MSC hits are about mesenchymal stem cells, not the TF; HR hits are 'hazard ratio' epidemiology). Blood-vs-brain-tumor immune surveillance is a plausible but not clinically established link, which is why this lands as unexpected rather than supported, and weak rather than insufficient — there is a real module to name, just no disease-specific record behind it.
support: none found — no retrieved paper documents RFXANK, MSC, or IRX2 in either fibromyalgia or lower-grade glioma; the retrieved MSC hits (e.g. PMIDs 40353645, 41484803, 39542476) concern mesenchymal stem cells or unrelated conditions (IBD), a name collision with the gene symbol, and are not evidence for this programme.
how_to_falsify: In matched PBMC samples from fibromyalgia patients and controls, and in matched LGG tumor vs adjacent tissue, measure HLA-DR surface/mRNA levels together with CXCL10/CCL5 secretion and FOXP3/CTLA4/IL2RA transcript levels; if RFXANK, MSC, and IRX2 expression/activity do not track with (or perturbing RFXANK does not move) MHC-II, Treg-gene, and chemokine output concordantly in both tissues, the proposed circuit is not operating as claimed for this pair.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) vs brain (LGG) — a systemic vs a local tumor-microenvironment readout, not the same cellular context. The 124 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts likely reflect limited independent replication, not 124 separate confirmations. The tissue-generic exclusion list already removed the obvious blood/brain immune master regulators (STAT1, IRF1, IRF5, NFATC1, ETS1/2, RELB, TWIST1, BCL6, GLI1, HLX, CREB5) — including the IFN-γ/STAT1→CIITA arm that would canonically sit upstream of RFXANK — so this account is built from what's left after the generic immune signal was stripped out, and should not be over-read as a full antigen-presentation-pathway story. ATF4 was excluded from the module despite a respectable comparison count because it is explicitly flagged discordant (target sets disagreed between the two diseases), not concordant like the others. HEY1/HES4/TCF12 form a separate, better-supported (higher count) Notch/bHLH progenitor-differentiation module among the concordant factors, but were not used here because their myogenic/neurogenic target genes (MYOG, ACTA2, COL2A1, NEUROD1, PAX6) are not realistically active programs in blood, making a blood-tissue story for them harder to defend than for the immune module chosen.
